summary: This note is the Humble-version user documentation for the ros2_control joint_trajectory_controller, which executes joint-space trajectories on a group of joints by interpolating between waypoints. It describes supported command and state interface combinations, other features such as real-time safety and wrapping-joint handling, a sample YAML configuration, and the preemption policy. It also documents the controller's action, topic, publisher and service interfaces and links to trajectory and parameter references.
one_line: User documentation for ROS 2's joint_trajectory_controller, covering trajectory execution, interface types, configuration and the controller's action, topic and service interfaces.
key_facts: The joint_trajectory_controller executes joint-space trajectories on a group of joints and interpolates in time between waypoints so their distance can be arbitrary.
Even trajectories with only one point are accepted by the joint_trajectory_controller.
Supported command interface combinations include position; position and velocity; position, velocity and acceleration; velocity; and effort.
For velocity and effort command interfaces, the position+velocity trajectory following error is mapped to commands through a PID loop if configured.
With command interface effort, state interfaces must include position and velocity.
The velocity state interface cannot be used if the position interface is missing.
The controller expects at least position feedback from the hardware; joint velocities and accelerations are optional.
The controller is realtime-safe and handles wrapping (continuous) joints properly.
Only one action goal can be active at any moment, or none if the topic interface is used.
Sending an empty trajectory message from the topic interface overrides the current action goal and does not abort the action.
The action interface is <controller_name>/follow_joint_trajectory with type control_msgs::action::FollowJointTrajectory.
The topic interface is <controller_name>/joint_trajectory with type trajectory_msgs::msg::JointTrajectory and is a fire-and-forget alternative.
The controller_state publisher uses control_msgs::msg::JointTrajectoryControllerState and publishes at the controller manager's update rate.
The query_state service is <controller_name>/query_state with type control_msgs::srv::QueryTrajectoryState and queries controller state at any future time.
The sample YAML configuration sets state_publish_rate to 50.0, action_monitor_rate to 20.0, allow_partial_joints_goal to false and open_loop_control to true.
The documentation is for ROS 2 Humble, and Iron is listed as the latest version.
